title: Animations and gestures
summary: The Animated API, the native driver, interpolation, layout animations and why animations should run on the UI thread.

sections.title: Animated values
sections.body: `Animated.Value` holds a number that drives styles without re-rendering React. `Animated.timing`, `spring` and `decay` change it over time, and `Animated.View` applies it. Combine animations with `sequence`, `parallel` and `stagger`.

sections.title: The native driver
sections.body: With `useNativeDriver: true`, the animation is sent to native code once and runs on the UI thread, so it stays smooth even when the JS thread is busy. It only supports non-layout properties: `transform` and `opacity`. Animating `width`, `height`, `top` or colors needs the JS driver (or a UI-thread animation library). Prefer `transform: [{ translateX }]` and `scale` over layout properties.

sections.title: Interpolation
sections.body:
`value.interpolate({ inputRange, outputRange })` maps one range onto another, piecewise linearly. Both ranges need the same length and `inputRange` must increase. `extrapolate` controls values outside the range: `extend` (the default) continues the line, `clamp` holds the end value and `identity` returns the input. Output can be numbers, colors or strings like `'45deg'`.

Exercises here run as TypeScript in a browser sandbox with no React Native runtime, so they model this logic as plain functions and reducers. The same functions drop straight into a real app: call them from a component, a hook or a store. The exercise implements numeric interpolation with each extrapolation mode.

sections.title: Gestures and UI-thread code
sections.body: Gesture libraries recognise pans, pinches and swipes natively. Animation libraries built on worklets run small JS functions on the UI thread, so a drag can follow the finger with no JS thread round trip. `LayoutAnimation` animates the next layout change for simple cases like expanding a row.

pitfalls: Animating `width` or `top` with `useNativeDriver: true`, which throws.
Creating `new Animated.Value` on every render instead of in a ref.
Driving a drag through `setState` on every move event.

gotchas.question: What is `x.interpolate({ inputRange: [0, 100], outputRange: [0, 1] })` when `x` is 150?
gotchas.answer: `1.5`, because the default extrapolation is `extend`. With `extrapolate: 'clamp'` it would be `1`.

gotchas.question: Why does an animation stutter while a list loads?
gotchas.answer: It runs on the JS thread, which is busy. Use `useNativeDriver: true` with transform or opacity so it runs on the UI thread.

gotchas.question: Can the native driver animate `backgroundColor`?
gotchas.answer: Not with the built-in Animated driver in most versions; it supports transform and opacity (and a few other non-layout props). Check the version, or animate on the UI thread with a worklet library.
